hyde: Any statute or portion thereof inconsistent with these rules is superseded to the extent of the inconsistency. Statutory provisions not addressed by these rules remain in full force and effect unless expressly repealed. The court shall apply statutory procedures where no rule governs, provided such application does not conflict with the intent or explicit language of these rules.

These rules shall be construed to secure the just, speedy, and inexpensive determination of every action. No error or defect in procedure or form shall invalidate any proceeding unless a party objects promptly and substantial prejudice results from the failure to comply with the rule. The court may disregard technical errors that do not affect substantial rights.

A case pending when these rules take effect shall be conducted under former rules unless the court orders otherwise. On motion by any party or sua sponte, the court may order that a pending case proceed under these rules if justice requires. The court’s determination is final and not subject to appeal.

Unless the court orders otherwise, singular terms include the plural and plural terms include the singular. A reference to a party includes all parties joined in the action. A reference to an affidavit includes multiple affidavits filed by any party. Gender references are interchangeable. This interpretation applies to all rules unless the context clearly requires a different meaning.

When the period of time prescribed or allowed is less than seven days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays shall be excluded in the computation. If the last day falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, the period continues until the end of the next day which is not a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday. The day of the act, event, or default from which the designated period begins to run is not included.

All documents filed electronically or generated by the court within the case management system constitute the official record of the proceeding. No paper counterpart is required for such documents to be part of the record. The court shall maintain these electronic records as the exclusive source for all filings and orders, unless a specific rule mandates physical preservation.

Discovery materials lodged with the clerk shall constitute part of the official court record. A party may move to strike such materials from the record for good cause shown. Unless otherwise ordered by the court, all filed discovery documents remain subject to public inspection and retention requirements applicable to other pleadings and papers on file.

The court record includes all documents filed with the clerk and all recordings made by the court. Information generated by the court’s case management and electronic filing systems is not part of the court record unless specifically incorporated by order. A party may move to include such system-generated information in the record on motion, showing good cause. The court shall rule on such motion within 14 days.

A party seeking specific pronoun usage or form of address shall state such preferences in the caption of any filed pleading. Upon motion, the court shall honor stated preferences in open court proceedings, provided the request is reasonable and does not disrupt judicial administration. Failure to include preferences in the caption waives the right to compel their use during hearings.

In every juvenile proceeding, the caption must include the phrase “Juvenile Proceeding” immediately following the case number. This designation is mandatory regardless of whether the action arises under the Juvenile Code or other statutes governing minors. Failure to include this identifier does not invalidate the filing but requires immediate correction upon notice by the court clerk.

The clerk shall redact Social Security numbers from all documents before providing copies to the public, including certified copies. This requirement applies regardless of the filing date or document type. Failure to redact constitutes a violation of privacy protections. Parties may move to unseal specific information only upon showing good cause.

Confidential data submitted on separate sheets shall be used solely for case identification and administrative purposes. Such data must not appear in chronological entries or public records. Court staff may not disclose, release, or use these identifiers for any purpose other than maintaining the integrity of the court’s internal filing system, unless expressly authorized by law or court order.

Before issuing a register of actions containing dates of birth, the clerk must verify that the requester is listed on the current state-approved roster for accessing such information. The clerk shall confirm the requester’s identity and authorization status prior to release. If the requester is not verified as authorized, the clerk must withhold the date of birth from the document provided.

On motion or sua sponte, the court shall order redaction of personal data identifiers from documents filed with the court. A party must file a redacted copy within 14 days after filing an unredacted document. The original document remains part of the record but is sealed from public inspection. Failure to comply may result in sanctions.
